entry.title: Finite-alphabet information rate-distortion function
entry.statement:
Let $\mathcal X,\widehat{\mathcal X}$ be nonempty finite alphabets, let $p$ be a pmf on $\mathcal X$, and let $d:\mathcal X\times\widehat{\mathcal X}\to[0,\infty)$ be finite-valued. A test channel is a stochastic matrix $W(\hat x\mid x)$, and its expected single-letter distortion is $\sum_{x,\hat x}p(x)W(\hat x\mid x)d(x,\hat x)$, with block distortion as in [[def-it-single-letter-distortion-and-block-distortion]]. Put $D_{\min}=\sum_xp(x)\min_{\hat x}d(x,\hat x)$. Define, in bits,
$$
R_{p,d}(D):=\begin{cases}\displaystyle\min_{W:\,\mathbb E d(X,\hat X)\le D} \frac{I(X;\hat X)}{\ln2},&D\ge D_{\min},\\[4pt]+\infty,&D<D_{\min}. \end{cases}
$$
The minimum exists by [[lem-it-finite-rate-distortion-minimum-attained]]. Values are not operational code rates; the finite memoryless coding theorem is a separate claim.
entry.strategy: Use the finite mutual-information and bit-conversion suppliers, define the feasible channel simplex and endpoint thresholds, and cite the local compactness lemma for minimum attainment.

entry.title: Fixed-length operational rate-distortion functions
entry.statement:
Let $X_0,X_1,\ldots$ be a source over a finite nonempty alphabet $\mathcal X$, let $\widehat{\mathcal X}$ be finite nonempty, and let $d:\mathcal X\times\widehat{\mathcal X}\to[0,\infty)$ be finite-valued. For positive integers $n$ and $M_n$, write $[M_n]=\{1,\ldots,M_n\}$. An $n$-block fixed-length code with $M_n$ messages is a deterministic encoder $f_n:\mathcal X^n\to[M_n]$ and decoder $g_n:[M_n]\to\widehat{\mathcal X}^{\,n}$; its reconstruction is $\widehat X^n=g_n(f_n(X^n))$, its block distortion is [[def-it-single-letter-distortion-and-block-distortion]], and its rate is $n^{-1}\log_2M_n$ bits per source symbol.

For each $D\ge0$, define the expected-distortion operational rate $R_{\mathrm{op}}^{\mathrm{avg}}(D)$ as the infimum of $\limsup_n n^{-1}\log_2M_n$ over code sequences satisfying $\limsup_n\mathbb E d_n(X^n,\widehat X^n)\le D$. Define the positive-slack excess-distortion operational rate $R_{\mathrm{op}}^{\mathrm{slack}}(D)$ by the same rate infimum over code sequences satisfying

$$\text{for every }\varepsilon>0,\qquad \mathbb P\!\left(d_n(X^n,\widehat X^n)>D+\varepsilon\right)\longrightarrow0.$$

The infimum of an empty set of admissible code sequences is $+\infty$. The expected and positive-slack excess criteria are separate definitions. An exact-threshold condition $\mathbb P(d_n>D)\to0$ is not part of either definition.
entry.strategy: State encoder, decoder, code rate, expected criterion, excess criterion with every positive slack, and infimum convention separately.

entry.title: Temperley–Lieb quantum integers and quantum characteristic
At zero loop value, rank three and rank four have opposite semisimplicity
Finite-IID rate-distortion mutual-information converse
entry.statement: For an IID finite-alphabet source and any finite block reconstruction with expected distortion D_k, proves ln(2) times the single-letter information rate-distortion value in bits is at most k^{-1} I(S^k;S-hat^k) in nats, by finite time-sharing and chain-rule single-letterization.
entry.strategy: Use the conditional reproduction test channel, the IID chain rule, coordinate projections, a uniform time-sharing index, and explicit bit-to-nat conversion.
proof_obligations: Construct the single-letter conditional reproduction channel induced by a uniformly chosen coordinate, including arbitrary rows on zero-probability source letters.
Show each coordinate mutual information is bounded by the corresponding chain-rule term using IID independence and nonnegative conditional mutual information.
Show mutual information of the time-shared pair is no larger than the average coordinate mutual information.
Apply the feasible-test-channel definition and convert bits to nats.

references.title: Yury Polyanskiy, MIT OpenCourseWare 6.441 Information Theory, Chapter 20: Advanced Channel Coding and Source-Channel Separation
Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, author-hosted full text

entry.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; all alphabets, conditional laws, and time-sharing variables are finite.

entry.title: Attainment of finite-alphabet rate-distortion minima
entry.statement:
Let $\mathcal X,\widehat{\mathcal X}$ be nonempty finite sets, let $p$ be a probability mass function on $\mathcal X$, and let $d:\mathcal X\times\widehat{\mathcal X}\to[0,\infty)$ be finite-valued. Put
$$
D_{\min}:=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p(x)\min_{\hat x\in\widehat{\mathcal X}}d(x,\hat x).
$$
For every $D\ge0$, the feasible stochastic channels $W(\hat x\mid x)$ satisfying $\sum_{x,\hat x}p(x)W(\hat x\mid x)d(x,\hat x)\le D$ form a nonempty set exactly when $D\ge D_{\min}$. Whenever nonempty, mutual information in bits attains its minimum over this set.
entry.strategy: Identify the minimum feasible distortion by pointwise minimization, use Heine–Borel for the closed channel slice, and prove continuity of the finite mutual-information objective at zero probabilities.

entry.title: Jones–Wenzl existence over a field is detected by one quantum-binomial row
entry.statement: Let $K$ be a field, $\delta\in K$, and $n\ge0$. A normalized idempotent $e\in\mathrm{TL}_n(K,\delta)$ with $d_ie=0$ for $1\le i<n$ exists if and only if every $B_{n,k}(\delta)$ of [[lem-temperley-lieb-quantum-binomial-digit-criterion]], $0\le k\le n$, is nonzero. Every such $e$ also satisfies $ed_i=0$ and is unique. This is a field assertion; it makes no integral-ring descent claim.

entry.title: Nonvanishing of an entire quantum-binomial row and the characteristic digits
entry.statement:
For $0\le k\le n$, let $G_{n,k}(Q)$ be the polynomial $\sum_w Q^{\operatorname{inv}(w)}$, summed over binary words with $k$ ones and $n-k$ zeros, where $\operatorname{inv}(w)$ counts pairs with a one to the left of a zero. There is a unique polynomial $B_{n,k}(T)\in\mathbb Z[T]$ such that

$$B_{n,k}(q+q^{-1})=q^{-k(n-k)}G_{n,k}(q^2).$$

It agrees as a rational-function identity with $[n]!/([k]![n-k]!)$; its value at a specialized loop parameter is the polynomial value, without division by vanishing factorials.

For a field $K$, $\delta\in K$, recurrence quantum characteristic $\ell$, and $p=\operatorname{char}K$, every $B_{n,k}(\delta)$ for $0\le k\le n$ is nonzero exactly as follows: if $\ell=\infty$, at every finite $n$; if $\ell<\infty$ and $p>0$, when $n<\ell$ or $n=a\ell p^{i-1}-1$ with $i\ge1$ and $1\le a<p$; if $\ell<\infty$ and $p=0$, when $n<\ell$ or $n=a\ell-1$ for a positive integer $a$.

entry.title: Finite-alphabet memoryless rate-distortion coding theorem
entry.statement: Let $(X_i)_{i\ge0}$ be iid with a pmf on a finite nonempty alphabet $\mathcal X$, let $\widehat{\mathcal X}$ be finite nonempty, and let $d:\mathcal X\times\widehat{\mathcal X}\to[0,d_{\max}]$ be finite nonnegative distortion. For every $D\ge0$, the expected-distortion and positive-slack excess-distortion operational rates of [[def-it-operational-rate-distortion-function]] both equal the finite information rate-distortion function of [[def-it-information-rate-distortion-function]], with value $+\infty$ when $D<D_{\min}$.
entry.strategy: Prove the converse by finite mutual-information data processing, single-letterization, convexity, and endpoint continuity; prove achievability by a random codebook, an information-density and distortion typical set, default reproduction, and diagonal limits.

entry.title: Lossy separation for finite IID sources and finite DMCs
entry.statement: For a finite IID source, finite reproduction alphabet, bounded finite distortion, feasible D, finite DMC capacity C nats/use, and channel-use ratio rho, let r(D)=ln(2)R(D) be the finite information rate-distortion function converted from bits to nats. Expected distortion and positive-slack excess-distortion criteria are separately achievable if r(D)<rho C, and either criterion implies r(D)<=rho C. If R(D)=0 a constant-reproduction code achieves both criteria; the positive-rate equality boundary is not asserted.
entry.strategy: Use the finite-alphabet rate-distortion coding theorem and maximal-error channel codes for achievability; use the local single-letter mutual-information converse, the n-letter DMC information bound, bounded distortion, monotonicity, and right-continuity for the converse.
proof_obligations: Treat the zero-rate RDF case by constructing an independent zero-information test channel and a constant reproduction whose expected distortion is at most D.
For positive RDF strictly below rho C, choose a source-code rate and a maximal-error channel-code rate with strict margin, then align the blocklengths.
Bound composed expected distortion by the source-code distortion plus d_max times maximal channel error; bound excess probability by a source excess event plus channel error.
Single-letterize arbitrary block mutual information using the local IID time-sharing lemma and compare it with nC.
Use bounded distortion to pass from positive-slack excess probability to an expected-distortion bound, then use right-continuity at D.
